newsitem.title: USA: MTel expects no repeat of message problem.
newsitem.headline: MTel expects no repeat of message problem.

text.p: Mobile Telecommunication Technologies Corp (MTel) said it expected no repeat of the bombardment of false messages received by tens of thousands of its Skytel pager customers early on Thursday.

"The problem was in inadvertently sending a message used as a code for broadcast news," Scott Hamilton, director of investor relations said. "We will certainly re-evaluate the procedures but don't expect it to ever happen again," he said.
He said 100,000 of MTel's 1.5 million U.S. customers were affected, receiving between 20 and 25 erroneous beeps from about 0816 EST/1316 GMT and again later in the morning.
Many of the SkyTel customers who take the news headline service provided to the company by Dow Jones & Co Inc were affected, he said.
Investment analyst Jeanine Oburchay of brokers Bear Stearns said she did not think the problem was serious.
"It is not indicative of MTel's ability to provide the service, I don't think it will hit their reputation," she said.
Many paging stocks were depressed in 1996 because of worries that new mobile phones with in-built pagers would take some of their market share.
In addition MTel itself was hit because its two-way paging service did not perform well at first, and was re-launched.
"The two-way service hasn't been the stellar performer we had hoped but acknowledgement paging should make up for that," Oburchay said.
Acknowledgement paging allows users to show those paging them that they have received messages. Oburchay expected it to be a big market in text message paging.
MTel shares were unchanged at $9 at 1225 EST/1725 GMT.
Meanwhile, customers said they were bombarded with false messages with phone numbers from across the country.
One customer said she received messages to call phone numbers from one end of the United States to another.
